problem.title: Design a Global URL Redirection Engine (100K RPS)

spark.summary: Design a globally distributed URL shortening and redirection engine serving 100K RPS reads (<15ms p99), 1K RPS writes, 5-year durability, and real-time click analytics.
spark.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, serve redirects from Anycast Edge POPs with L1 LRU + regional Redis, coordinate writes via pre-allocated Base62 key-range shards, and replicate asynchronously across regions.
spark.byteSummary:
A Global URL Redirection Engine is an ultra-read-heavy system (100:1 read/write ratio: 100K RPS reads vs. 1K RPS writes) requiring <15ms global p99 redirect latency and 99.99% availability. Over 5 years at 1K writes/sec, the store accumulates ~158 billion URLs (~80TB of raw mapping data).

The architecture spans: (1) Anycast Edge POPs running L1 in-memory LRU caches backed by regional Redis Clusters to serve 95%+ of redirects without crossing WANs; (2) a Multi-Region Write Coordinator leasing disjoint Base62 key-range shards from ZooKeeper/etcd so regions never collide; (3) an Active-Active geo-replicated Cassandra/DynamoDB store with Safe-Browsing phishing checks and TTL expiration; and (4) a Clickstream Kafka + Apache Flink pipeline powering real-time geo/referrer analytics.

Key trade-offs include using asynchronous multi-region replication (eventual consistency of ~1-2s on new links, or read-your-writes sticky routing for the creator) to avoid cross-continent write consensus latency.

learningJourney.title: Traffic & 5-Year Storage Sizing
learningJourney.purpose: Calculate read/write QPS, 5-year storage footprint, and Redis cache memory.

explanation.core: At ~500 bytes per record (short_code, long_url, user_id, created_at, expires_at), raw data is ~79TB (with 3x replication = ~237TB).
explanation.deepDive: Applying the 80/20 rule for 100K RPS reads: caching the hot 20% of daily active links (~17M links * 500B = ~8.5GB) fits easily inside a modest regional Redis cluster.

cards.label: Bandwidth

learningJourney.title: Anycast Edge POPs & L1/L2 Regional Caching
learningJourney.purpose: Achieve <15ms global p99 redirect latency across continents.

explanation.foundation: Anycast BGP routes users to the nearest Edge POP.
explanation.core: Each POP maintains an L1 in-memory LRU cache (100K hottest global slugs, <0.2ms) and queries a regional L2 Redis Cluster (<2ms) on L1 miss.
explanation.deepDive: Only the ~2% long-tail cold misses traverse to the regional Cassandra/DynamoDB replica, keeping global p99 redirect latency under 15ms.

sectionDiagram.title: Anycast POP + L1/L2 Cache Hierarchy

cards.label: Viral Absorption
cards.detail: L1 LRU absorbs 50K+ RPS single-link spikes without hitting Redis.

cards.label: Negative Cache
cards.detail: Edge Bloom filters + 60s 404 cache block invalid-code floods.

sectionDiagram.summary: Three-tier Anycast + L1 + L2 caching keeps 98% of redirects within the local metro region.
sectionDiagram.caption: Local NoSQL replicas ensure cold reads never cross oceans.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Global URL Redirection Engine (100K RPS) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, serve redirects from Anycast Edge POPs with L1 LRU + regional Redis, coordinate writes via pre-allocated Base62 key-range shards, and replicate asynchronously across regions.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Design a Global URL Redirection Engine (100K RPS) experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Multi-Region Write Coordinator & Key-Range Shards
learningJourney.purpose: Generate globally unique short codes across US, EU, and APAC with zero cross-region locks.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Multi-Region Write Coordinator & Key-Range Shards** as the intuition layer for Design a Global URL Redirection Engine (100K RPS): Generate globally unique short codes across US, EU, and APAC with zero cross-region locks.
explanation.core: Running cross-continent Paxos on every `POST /shorten` would add 150ms+ write latency. Instead, a central ZooKeeper/etcd coordinator assigns disjoint prefix ranges to each region (e.g., `a-g*` to US, `h-n*` to EU, `o-z*` to APAC), and regional write workers lease 1M-ID sub-blocks locally—generating globally unique codes in <1ms.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, multi-region write coordinator & key-range shards becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Optimize edge-batched Kafka + Flink GDPR clickstreams, partition-key TTL compaction, and Bloom-filter 404 shielding.

sectionDiagram.title: Disjoint Regional Key-Range Shards

cards.label: Zero Cross-WAN Write
cards.detail: Regions issue short codes completely independently with zero WAN round-trips.

cards.label: Custom Vanity Slugs
cards.detail: Only user-chosen custom aliases use conditional quorum writes (LWT/ConditionalPut).

sectionDiagram.summary: Disjoint regional key-range shards eliminate cross-region consensus from the standard write path.
sectionDiagram.caption: Custom vanity aliases are isolated to conditional writes without slowing auto-generated links.

learningJourney.title: Active-Active Geo-Replicated NoSQL & Read-Your-Writes
learningJourney.purpose: Replicate mappings globally while ensuring a creator's immediate test click never 404s.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Active-Active Geo-Replicated NoSQL & Read-Your-Writes** as the intuition layer for Design a Global URL Redirection Engine (100K RPS): Replicate mappings globally while ensuring a creator's immediate test click never 404s.
explanation.core: Cassandra (NetworkTopologyStrategy) or DynamoDB Global Tables replicates writes asynchronously across regions in ~1-2s. To prevent a creator from hitting a 404 if they click their new link within 200ms in a different POP, the write response sets a short-lived regional affinity hint (or writes-through to the creator's local L2 Redis) and cold misses fall back cross-region once before returning 404.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, active-active geo-replicated nosql & read-your-writes becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Optimize edge-batched Kafka + Flink GDPR clickstreams, partition-key TTL compaction, and Bloom-filter 404 shielding.

sectionDiagram.title: Active-Active NoSQL + Cross-Region Fallback

cards.label: First-Char Hint
cards.detail: The slug's first character encodes its origin region, making 1x fallback routing exact.

cards.label: Bounded Fallback
cards.detail: Only fall back for keys passing the Bloom filter or within 10s of creation.

sectionDiagram.summary: Encoding origin region in the prefix enables exact single-hop fallback during replication lag.
sectionDiagram.caption: Write-through to local Redis guarantees instant read-your-writes in the creator's region.

learningJourney.title: Safe-Browsing Phishing Scanner & Abuse Takedown
learningJourney.purpose: Block malicious destinations at creation time and propagate takedowns globally in seconds.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Safe-Browsing Phishing Scanner & Abuse Takedown** as the intuition layer for Design a Global URL Redirection Engine (100K RPS): Block malicious destinations at creation time and propagate takedowns globally in seconds.
explanation.core: On `POST /shorten`, the Write Worker checks the destination domain/URL against an in-memory Safe-Browsing prefix hash list (<1ms) and rejects known malware/phishing with `400 Bad Request`. An async crawler inspects newly created links for redirect chains/phishing kits; confirmed abusers trigger a Redis Pub/Sub cache invalidation across all Edge POPs and mark the DB row `BANNED`.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, safe-browsing phishing scanner & abuse takedown becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Optimize edge-batched Kafka + Flink GDPR clickstreams, partition-key TTL compaction, and Bloom-filter 404 shielding.

sectionDiagram.title: Sync Blocklist + Global Cache Purge

cards.label: Fast Takedown
cards.detail: Global Pub/Sub purge evicts malicious L1/L2 cache entries across POPs within 2 seconds.

cards.label: Rate-Limited Writes
cards.detail: Apply strict per-IP/API-key token buckets on POST /shorten to stop spam bots.

sectionDiagram.summary: Combining sub-millisecond sync blocklists with async deep scanning stops abuse without slowing writes.
sectionDiagram.caption: Global Pub/Sub cache purges enforce takedowns across all Edge POPs in seconds.

learningJourney.title: Clickstream Kafka + Flink Real-Time Analytics
learningJourney.purpose: Deliver live click counts, geo maps, and bot-filtered unique visitors at 100K RPS.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Clickstream Kafka + Flink Real-Time Analytics** as the intuition layer for Design a Global URL Redirection Engine (100K RPS): Deliver live click counts, geo maps, and bot-filtered unique visitors at 100K RPS.
explanation.core: Each Edge POP batches click events asynchronously to regional Kafka clusters (`short_clicks`). Apache Flink jobs filter known bot User-Agents, enrich IP prefixes with MaxMind GeoIP (dropping raw IPs for GDPR), and compute 1-minute tumbling aggregations + HyperLogLog unique counts into ClickHouse.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, clickstream kafka + flink real-time analytics becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Optimize edge-batched Kafka + Flink GDPR clickstreams, partition-key TTL compaction, and Bloom-filter 404 shielding.

sectionDiagram.title: Edge-Batched Kafka + Flink Pipeline

cards.label: GDPR Compliance
cards.detail: Strip raw IP addresses inside Flink right after GeoIP lookup.

cards.label: Zero Redirect Impact
cards.detail: Drop analytics buffers gracefully if Kafka backs up; never delay 302s.

sectionDiagram.summary: Edge-batched Kafka ingestion and Flink enrichment scale analytics to 100K RPS cleanly.
sectionDiagram.caption: Dropping raw IPs after GeoIP lookup keeps clickstream analytics privacy-compliant.

learningJourney.title: TTL Expiration Engine & Tombstone Compaction
learningJourney.purpose: Support expiring campaign links without degrading Cassandra read performance.

explanation.foundation: Links with `expires_at` store the timestamp in the payload and leverage Cassandra/DynamoDB TTLs.
explanation.core: Reading an expired cached entry checks `now > expires_at` lazily and returns `410 Gone`.
explanation.deepDive: To avoid Cassandra tombstone scan stalls on range queries, queries are strictly point-lookups by partition key (`short_code`), and compaction runs with `tombstone_threshold` tuning.

sectionDiagram.title: Point-Lookup TTL & Tombstone Cleanup

cards.label: Point-Lookup Safety
cards.detail: Partitioning by short_code avoids multi-row tombstone scans.

cards.label: 410 Gone
cards.detail: Returning 410 lets Edge CDNs cache the expired state and stop origin hits.

sectionDiagram.summary: Lazy expiration checks and partition-key point lookups keep TTL cleanup fast and safe.
sectionDiagram.caption: Caching 410 Gone responses prevents expired links from hitting origin databases.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does a Multi-Region URL Shortener generate globally unique short codes without paying 150ms+ cross-continent consensus latency on every write?

options.text: Assign disjoint Base62 prefix shards per region and lease 1M-ID blocks locally from regional ZooKeeper/etcd.
options.feedback: Correct! Disjoint regional prefix shards guarantee global uniqueness with zero cross-WAN coordination per write.

options.text: Run a single PostgreSQL primary in US-East for all global writes.
options.feedback: A single primary forces 150ms+ WAN round-trips for EU and APAC writers.

options.text: Use random 4-character strings without checking for collisions.
options.feedback: 4-character random strings would collide constantly due to the birthday paradox.

options.text: Disable writes in EU and APAC.
options.feedback: Multi-region write availability is a core requirement.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Partitioning the key space by region (e.g., `[a-g]*`, `[h-n]*`, `[o-z]*`) lets each region generate unique slugs locally in <1ms.

knowledgeChecks.question: A creator in London shortens a URL and immediately tests it from an Edge POP, hitting an EU replica before async geo-replication completes. How can the engine prevent a false 404?

options.text: Encode the origin region in the slug prefix and perform a single fallback lookup to the origin region on a cold miss.
options.feedback: Correct! Origin-encoded prefixes allow exact single-hop fallback during the ~1s replication window.

options.text: Tell the user to wait 5 minutes before clicking their link.
options.feedback: Poor UX when immediate read-your-writes is expected.

options.text: Force synchronous 3-continent Paxos on every click.
options.feedback: Synchronous cross-continent reads would destroy the <15ms redirect SLA.
Redirecting to the wrong URL is a severe bug.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Encoding the origin region in the slug prefix lets a cold miss check the origin region once before returning 404, bridging async replication lag.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should clickstream analytics events be emitted asynchronously to Kafka rather than written synchronously to ClickHouse during a 302 redirect?

options.text: To keep redirect latency under 15ms and ensure analytics backpressure never causes 302 redirect outages.
options.feedback: Correct! Decoupling analytics via non-blocking Kafka batches protects the critical redirect path.
ClickHouse handles timestamps natively; the reason is latency and fault isolation.

options.text: Because 302 redirects do not carry HTTP headers.
options.feedback: 302 requests carry standard headers like User-Agent and Referer.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Users expect instant redirects. Offloading analytics to non-blocking Kafka batches isolates redirect availability from analytics load.

beginner.summary: Design a global URL shortener like Bitly that handles 100,000 redirects per second across the world.
beginner.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, serve redirects from Anycast Edge POPs with L1 LRU + regional Redis, coordinate writes via pre-allocated Base62 key-range shards, and replicate asynchronously across regions.
beginner.byteSummary:
At 100,000 clicks per second, speed comes from caching links as close to users as possible using Edge POPs and Redis. To create new links fast without regions clashing, each region gets its own starting letter range.

Click tracking is sent in the background to Kafka so users get redirected in under 15 milliseconds.

intermediate.summary: Architect 100K RPS Anycast L1/L2 caching, disjoint Base62 regional shards, active-active NoSQL, and Safe-Browsing checks.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, serve redirects from Anycast Edge POPs with L1 LRU + regional Redis, coordinate writes via pre-allocated Base62 key-range shards, and replicate asynchronously across regions.
intermediate.byteSummary:
Anycast Edge POPs pair L1 in-memory LRU caches with regional Redis Clusters to serve 98% of 100K RPS reads locally in <15ms. Multi-region write coordinators lease disjoint Base62 prefix shards (`[a-g]*`, `[h-n]*`, `[o-z]*`) so regions write locally with zero WAN locks.

Active-active Cassandra/DynamoDB replicates globally, with origin-encoded prefixes enabling single-hop fallback on fresh misses and Pub/Sub purges enforcing phishing takedowns in seconds.

advanced.summary: Optimize edge-batched Kafka + Flink GDPR clickstreams, partition-key TTL compaction, and Bloom-filter 404 shielding.
advanced.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, serve redirects from Anycast Edge POPs with L1 LRU + regional Redis, coordinate writes via pre-allocated Base62 key-range shards, and replicate asynchronously across regions.
advanced.byteSummary:
Edge POPs emit batched click events to Kafka, where Apache Flink filters bots, enriches MaxMind GeoIP, drops raw IPs for GDPR, and updates HyperLogLog unique counters in ClickHouse.

Point-lookup partitioning by `short_code` prevents Cassandra tombstone scan stalls during TTL compaction, while Edge Bloom filters and 410 Gone caching protect origins from invalid-code floods.
